"The search for Vijaya Lakshmi Gali, an Indian tourist who fell into a sinkhole in Kuala Lumpur on 23 August, has been suspended due to safety concerns. The incident occurred when the pavement collapsed beneath her, causing her to disappear into an 8-meter-deep hole. Despite extensive efforts, rescuers have only recovered her slippers, with no further signs of her whereabouts. The operation involved advanced technology and tracker dogs, but the risks became too significant to continue.

Authorities cited the dangers to rescue personnel as the primary reason for halting the search. High-pressure water jets and excavators were used to clear debris from the underground drainage system, but conditions remained hazardous. Divers attempted to enter the sinkhole but were quickly withdrawn due to the unstable environment. The situation was further complicated by reports of a previous soil slip in the same area last year.

The decision to stop the search was announced by Dr. Zaliha Mustafa, a minister in the prime minister’s department. She emphasized the importance of prioritizing the well-being of the rescue team. The operation had entered its eighth day when officials concluded that proceeding would pose unacceptable risks. The lack of progress and the unstable conditions left little room for further action.

* The search was called off after divers were unable to safely navigate the sinkhole, highlighting the severe challenges faced by the rescue team.

Despite the setback, the efforts to locate Vijaya Lakshmi Gali were comprehensive, utilizing various methods to explore the underground system. The incident has raised concerns about the safety of infrastructure in the area, particularly given the history of similar events. Authorities may need to reassess the stability of the location to prevent future occurrences.

Is there anything else I can help with?"
